title: Regional shift safetyproof runbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft runbook for 'safetyproof' regional traffic shifts — the pattern we use when evacuating or pre-emptively draining a region while preserving low-latency traffic, cache consistency, and application correctness. It focuses on: staged DNS/traffic weight changes, KV/cache pre-seeding, graceful connection handoff, and observability gates.

Scope / When to use:
- Planned maintenance that requires >30% regional capacity reduction.
- Gradual evacuation when edge peer degradation crosses alert thresholds.
- Emergency soft-evacuation where we must keep core control plane available while shifting user traffic.

Non-goals:
- Full disaster recovery runbook (this is *traffic-shift focused* not restore procedures).
- Network-level BGP engineering — coordinate with netops for BGP-scale actions.

Key principles (safetyproof):
1) Observable gates: every step requires green health signals (latency, error-rate, KV hit-rate) before proceeding.
2) Reverse-first: always plan and test rollback path before applying a step.
3) Warm pre-seed: ensure caches and stateful frontends in target region are pre-warmed with realistic prefixes.
4) Narrow windows: prefer many small increments over one big cut.
5) Circuit-breaker alignment: client SDKs should detect regional failover and backoff; server-side circuit breakers must be coordinated.

Readiness checklist (pre-flight):
- [ ] Incident manager assigned and Slack channel pinned.
- [ ] Target region capacity confirmed (pods/GPU/instances) and autoscale enabled.
- [ ] KV cache replication job scheduled and test logs show < 5% transient misses for sampled keys.
- [ ] Canaries defined: 5% of traffic routed to target region should exercise worst-case paths.
- [ ] Route53/Cloud DNS weighted entries editable and pre-auth tokens available.
- [ ] Observability dashboards open: edge-latency, api-5xx, kv-hit-rate, prefix-ttl-miss, p95-token-latency.

Signals that trigger an evacuation: (examples)
- Edge peering loss > 50% for 5m in region-A AND origin 5xx spike > 3x baseline.
- Sustained KV replication lag > 30s for more than 2m.
- Operator judgment after failed mitigation attempts.

Staged run (operator steps):
0) Start incident channel, record start time, and capture baseline metrics (query snapshots).
1) Set 'safety mode' flags for client SDK routing (if supported) so clients will prefer fallback region earlier.
2) Pre-seed KV/warm cache flows:
   - Kick the prewarm job for top-10k active prefixes: /ops/preseed-kv job --region target --prefix-file s3://ops/top-prefixes-2025-02-15.csv
   - Monitor preseed progress: PromQL: sum(kv_preseed_in_progress{job="preseed"}) and kv_node_hitrate by region.
   - Goal: target region kv_hit_rate >= 85% for sampled prefixes before shifting more than 10% traffic.
3) Small weighted DNS shift (10% -> 25%):
   - Update DNS provider to add weighted entry for target region with 10% weight. If provider supports session affinity, preserve it.
   - If using edge LB weights, do the equivalent there.
   - Wait 3x DNS TTL or validate via active clients to confirm distribution.
4) Run synthetic smoke test traffic from multiple edge locations to confirm correctness and p99 latency targets.
5) Observe for 10 minutes for errors, kv miss spikes, or backend CPU pressure. If all clear, increment to 25%, then 50% with the same observation windows.
6) If errors appear: roll back to previous weight, mark incident note, perform troubleshooting (see Troubleshooting section), and iterate.

DNS specifics and TTL guidance:
- Use short TTLs for run (60s) where supported, but be mindful of rate limits on provider APIs.
- Prefer weighted records over hard CNAME swaps when possible to allow precise increments.
- If using regional CNAMEs to edge stacks, ensure the edge config in the target region accepts the new host header and TLS certs are valid.

KV / Cache consistency notes:
- Conservative approach: do not shift more than (kv_current_hit_rate_target - 10%) of traffic without preseed target.
- Preseed must include: session affinity keys, recent conversational contexts for active users, and per-tenant routing tags when used.
- If state drift is observed, enable read-fallback: on miss, attempt to fetch from origin synchronously (costly) with circuit-breaker to avoid cascading origin load.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- >2x baseline 5xx rate sustained for 3m.
- p95 latency > SLO threshold for >5m.
- KV miss rate spike > 3x baseline for >2m and not trending down.
If any triggered: immediately revert DNS/weights to last known-good and notify netops.

Monitoring queries (examples):
- API error rate (region-specific): sum(increase(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",region=~".*"}[5m])) by (region)
- KV hit rate: sum(kv_hits_total{region=~".*"}) / sum(kv_requests_total{region=~".*"})
- Replica lag (if using async replication): max(kv_replication_lag_seconds{region=~".*"})
- Client affinity breakage: count(client_conn_new_region{changed_region="true"})

Troubleshooting patterns (quick guide):
- Symptom: sudden p50/p95 latency jump in target region post-shift
  - Check: CPU/GPU utilization on frontends, replica lag, network egress saturation.
  - Action: throttle new connections via LB weight rollback and scale up frontends if autoscale not catching up.
- Symptom: backend 5xx only for subset of tenants
  - Check: per-tenant feature flags, certs, and routing tags in request headers.
  - Action: route that tenant back to origin region (route override) while other tenants stay shifted.
- Symptom: DNS does not converge to expected weights
  - Check: provider rate-limits, previous TTLs still in caches. Consider using client pinning flush endpoints or perform smaller increments and wait longer.

Post-incident capture (to fill in after run):
- Start/End timestamps:
- Triggering signal summary:
- Sequence of weight changes (time, %), preseed windows, and canary outcomes:
- Observed impacts (latency, errors, KV misses) by region:
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
- What worked, what didn't:
- Action items (owners + due dates) for automation, telemetry, or config changes:

Open experiments and automation backlog (ideas to reduce ops overhead):
- Automated preseed job that takes traffic samples and seeds only 'hot' prefixes with rollback safety flag.
- A small API for real-time weighted-shifts that rate-limits changes and enforces observability gates before commit.
- Route53 provider adapter that supports dry-run and TTL-preview.

Unresolved questions (for follow-up):
- Verify client SDK behavior for region affinity when weighted DNS changes mid-session (Daniel to test with synthetic long-lived connections).
- Should we build a declarative 'traffic-shift plan' CRD in cluster to coordinate LB weights + dns + kv preseed? (deps: platform eng)

Appendix: quick operator commands
- Preseed kick: kubectl -n ops run preseed-$(date +%s) --image=ops/preseed:stable --args "--region=eu-west-1 --prefix-file=s3://ops/top-prefixes.csv"
- Check kv hitrate: curl -s "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(kv_hits_total%7Bregion%3D%5E~.%2A%24%7D)%20/%20sum(kv_requests_total%7Bregion%3D%5E~.%2A%24%7D)" | jq .
- Update weighted DNS (example): aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://weight-change.json

Notes and provenance:
- Drafted 2025-02-15 during a regional edge degradation sim.
- Iterated after runbook tabletop on 2025-02-26.
- Owner: Aisha Kapoor; reviewers: Daniel Wu, Mariana Silva.

Status: draft — please add concrete test results and attach run transcripts after the next live exercise.
